facts.quote: Concession/restroom buildings Paved walking/hiking trails (2.35 miles)

Trail access can be found behind Holmes High School at the corner of Levassor and Eastern Ave. Additional locations to access the trail include the dead end of E. 16th Street, Clayton-Meyer Park and behind Randolph Park.

facts.text: The current city listing gives 1.5 miles of nature trail, 0.75 mile of paved trail and about 2.5 miles using sidewalks and roads. These published segment figures do not establish a continuous paved route.
facts.quote: Covington's trail includes 1.5 miles of nature trail, .75 miles of paved trails, and approximately 2.5 miles of trail utilizing sidewalk and road infrastructure.

facts.text: The city’s September 2019 completion article describes parallel upper-levee paved trail (about 0.75 mile) and lower riverside gravel nature trail (about 1.5 miles). It calls the whole Greenway 2.5 miles including sidewalks/roads. Confirm distance and surface before choosing a route.
facts.quote: Most of that stretch includes parallel trails – about 0.75 miles of paved trail atop the levee and about 1.5 miles of a gravel “nature trail” that cuts through a narrow stretch of woods along the river’s edge.
All told, the LRGT is 2.5 miles long, including sidewalk and road infrastructure.

facts.text: The county lists two large reservable shelters with electricity, a water fountain and a grill at each. The page does not describe wheelchair spaces, table clearances, shelter approaches or seasonal water availability.
facts.quote: Central Park has two large shelters available to reserve. Each shelter includes: Electricity Water fountain Grill
